cases.decision: lock-free pooled reqwest Client, RwLock read guard dropped at semicolon, outside-lock map drop, rayon::spawn + oneshot offload and single-statement UNNEST batch insert retained
checks: Verifies reqwest::Client is used directly via &self and drains the scale body before CPU work, rules uses RwLock with org_rules dropping the read guard at the let semicolon and replace_rules dropping the old map after unlocking, rayon::spawn + oneshot offloads par_iter without blocking Tokio worker or blocking-pool threads, and UNNEST batches all inserts atomically in one constant prepared statement
Reports no contention, executor-blocking or N-round-trip finding

cases.decision: Compute every shard directly from the byte length.
checks: Shows every entry originates solely from the key length; a hit hashes a tenant to avoid reading its length and taking a fixed remainder.
Removes the table and its lookups, preserving output order, multiplicity, empty and UTF-8 names and the original integer expression. Changing only the hasher misses the saving.

cases.decision: Keep the direct per-tenant calculation.
checks: Recognizes constant work per output apart from materializing the required return values.
Does not introduce memoization for repeated names or deduplicate ordered results.

cases.decision: The command-local snapshot keeps a second strong owner alive through every successful edit, copying the entire flags slice even when readers are absent
checks: Traces the handle clone in snapshot and the distinct payload copy in make_mut. The local Snapshot survives its last length read. For S slots and K successful toggles without readers, that lifetime causes K copies of S bytes, including N squared bytes for N commands on an N-slot board.
Borrows the length directly or ends the local snapshot before mutation. Keeps the invalid-index error, immediate bit toggle and any immutable snapshots held by external readers.

cases.decision: Unique ownership permits an in-place toggle and a reader of the current version requires detachment on the first successful edit
checks: Follows the reader-held strong handle to the original version. Its first overlapping edit must preserve those bytes, and later edits can be in place while the reader continues to hold the already-detached version. The fixed-length image changes at one byte, with no intermediate buffer.
Traces rejection before mutation and reports no avoidable repeated payload copy on the sole-owner path.

cases.decision: The timed-out reply waiter keeps tracking batch progress after losing its only result consumer.
checks: Traces timeout dropping the owned join handle: its final_total task can keep a watch subscription and wake on progress changes until the feed finishes or closes. The separate ledger task already delivers the required receipt.

Stops or eliminates only the reply waiter, preserving independent ledger delivery after deadline or caller departure and the caller's success, closed-feed, deadline and worker-error outcomes. Credit a supported tradeoff when earlier receiver drop changes what the producer can observe; watch notifications can coalesce.

cases.decision: Keep the shared completion worker alive after its caller times out.
checks: Follows final_total through ledger.send(total): the same worker supplies both the response and an independently awaited completion receipt, including when the caller stops waiting.
Recognizes that aborting the worker on timeout or caller departure can lose the ledger receipt. The caller's deadline can still bound its own wait.

cases.decision: quadratic front Vec::drain per frame replaced with cursor offset and single compaction
checks: Traces self.buf.drain(..frame_len) shifting all remaining buffered bytes down to index 0 on every decoded frame (O(K * N) bytes copied across up to 1,000 frames per chunk)

Proposes advancing a read offset across frames and clearing or compacting self.buf at most once on exit (including error paths), preserving FrameError::FrameTooLarge, pending_bytes(), and partial-frame retention

cases.decision: cursor-offset frame decoder with single end-of-batch compaction retained
checks: Verifies FrameDecoder::decode_all advances offset in O(1) per frame, clears in O(1) when consumed, compacts trailing partial bytes at most once, and skips compaction when offset is 0
Reports no complexity finding
